COURSE TITLE    POLITICAL SCIENCE III: POLITICAL PHILOSOPHY
COURSE CODE     10BH1302
COURSE CREDITS  3

Objective:
 1  To impart knowledge of ancient, medieval and modern streams of political thought in the
    West. •
 2  To make students aware about political thought, especially its inception and evolution. • To
    throw light on different views on human nature and the uses of history that inform the
     design of government
 3  To gain a critical perspective on our times by evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of
     various regimes and philosophical approaches.


Course Outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to:
 1  Define and Relate the principal modes of political thought.
 2  Outline political thought through the Classical, Renaissance, and Enlightenment periods
    based on the works of Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau,
     Tocqueville, and Marx.
 3  Dissect the differences between Plato and Aristotle with regard to their understandings of
     the nature of the person, ethics, society, citizenship, and governance.
 4  Measure the historical and intellectual context in which the western political thought helped
     to develop the modern nation-state.


Pre-requisite of course:N/A
